description: Phenotype definition for NHANES 2017-2020 diabetes prediction. Cross-sectional survey design: all labs, vitals, and questionnaires collected at a single exam visit. Target defined by HbA1c >= 6.5% OR self-reported doctor-diagnosed diabetes.

study_design.survey_weights_justification: Weights excluded intentionally. NHANES oversamples minorities; unweighted analysis is valid for internal prediction model development but prevalence estimates are not population-representative. External validation on differently-sampled cohorts is required.

diabetes.post_prediction_justification: Lipid panels (TCHOL_J, HDL_J, TRIGLY_J) are drawn at the same NHANES exam visit as HbA1c (GHB_J). Since HbA1c >= 6.5% defines the target, same-visit metabolic labs reflect post-diagnosis metabolic state and cannot be assumed available at a hypothetical pre-diagnosis prediction time point.
diabetes.prediction_time_justification: NHANES is cross-sectional. The clinically meaningful prediction scenario is screening: predicting diabetes risk using demographics, lifestyle, and vitals available before lab results are returned.

variable_notes.age: RIDAGEYR: top-coded at 80 (all >=80 mapped to 80). 7.1% of sample affected. Age-risk gradient compressed above 80.
variable_notes.race_ethnicity: RIDRETH3: NOMINAL categorical (not ordinal). Encoded as string labels to prevent numeric ordering. 1=Mexican American, 2=Other Hispanic, 3=NH White, 4=NH Black, 6=NH Asian, 7=Other/Multi-Racial.
variable_notes.sbp_mean_dbp_mean: BPXOSY2-3, BPXODI2-3: Average of readings 2 and 3 ONLY. Reading 1 excluded per NHANES protocol (white-coat effect). Reference: CDC NHANES Blood Pressure Procedures Manual.
variable_notes.ever_smoked: SMQ020: 'Smoked at least 100 cigarettes in entire life?' Threshold is 100 cigarettes (~5 packs), NOT 'ever tried smoking'.
variable_notes.bp_medication: BPQ050A: 'Now taking prescribed BP medicine?' Gated question — only asked if BPQ020=Yes (ever told high BP). NaN explicitly filled with 0 (no HTN diagnosis → no medication).
variable_notes.hypertension_diagnosed: BPQ020: 'Ever told you had high blood pressure?' Asked to all adults. Upstream gate for bp_medication.
variable_notes.family_history_diabetes: MCQ300C: 'Close relative had diabetes?' (parent, sibling). NOT DIQ172 which is subjective risk perception.
variable_notes.coronary_heart_disease: MCQ160C: 'Ever told had coronary heart disease?' Self-report, lifetime cumulative. Reverse causation possible (DM→CHD, not CHD→DM). Documented as limitation.
variable_notes.stroke: MCQ160F: 'Ever told had stroke?' Same reverse causation caveat as CHD.

known_limitations: Age top-coded at 80 — risk gradient compressed for elderly
2019-2020 cycle incomplete due to COVID-19 pandemic interruption
Survey weights not used — prevalence not population-representative
CHD and stroke features have reverse causation risk (DM→CVD possible)
Self-report variables subject to recall bias and social desirability bias
Target definition uses 2 evidence layers (lab + self-report); no ICD codes or medication records available for 3-layer adjudication
